notes: The question set for the knowledge pack (docs/RAG_PLAN.md step 1.4), scored by scripts/kb-eval.ts. Agent-written draft (decision D8); the owner may edit any entry at any time.

Each question was written from a need first; its expected records were then found by reading the sources (cards, rulings, decks, deck notes, packages, glossary, guides, docs, code headers, rules), not by taking a search result.

expect: every record that answers the question on its own. A question is found at k when any one of them is in the first k results. An entry ending in * accepts any passage of one doc section (later passages end in ~2, ~3).

scope: public, or local when only a rules, tournament-rules, errata or official FAQ record (data/raw, never tracked) answers it. A checkout without data/raw skips local questions and counts them as skipped. Rules questions are in our own words and store ids only.

type: entity (a name or part of one, as people type it), paraphrase (the thing asked for without the words of its title), cross (the answer is one link away: a card's rulings or packages, a deck's plan, the decks that play a card), dev (this codebase and its docs), rules (the game's rules, local scope).

number (q101 onward, plan step 2.2): a question whose answer is a number or a result from the recorded tournaments (a champion, a round's results, a rating, a tier, a matchup, a count). It expects the measured record that holds the answer (event, round, rating or matchup); the number itself comes from code (`npm run kb -- fact`), never from the search. Written from the need first, before the records were searched.

none (q117 onward, plan step 1.6): a question the pack cannot answer (a card that does not exist, another game, prices, real-world dates, accounts, apps, shops), with expect []. It is scored by refusal: the share of none questions for which the search says "no match". None questions are left out of recall and MRR; an answerable question the search refuses is counted as wrongly refused.

Step 1.6 also added rules questions q129-q138 (written after the step 1.4 totals had informed the rules idea, so they are fresh held-out questions for it) and number questions q139-q146 in phrasings the step 2.2 cue words do not cover ("how does X do against Y", "does X beat Y", "which decks are strongest", "who is top of the ratings"). q141 and q146 also expect the rating record of the deck first in src/data/ratings.json now: when the ratings are rebuilt and another deck leads, correct that id.
Split rule: within each type, in file order, the question at position i (0-based) is test when i mod 5 is 1 or 3, dev otherwise. That puts 40% of every type in test.
Rule M9: tune on dev, report on test. Once written, a question is never reworded to raise a score; only a wrong expect is corrected, and each correction is listed in the step's report.
